universe.title: Star Trek 4X Universe
universe.description: The Star Trek 4X universe encompasses the Alpha and Beta Quadrants of the Milky Way galaxy, featuring the major powers of the Star Trek universe in a grand strategy context. Players explore, expand, exploit, and exterminate across the stars while navigating the complex political landscape of the Federation, Klingons, Romulans, and other factions.
source_material: Star Trek original series and films

prime_directive.description: The Prime Directive, also known as General Order 1, is the most fundamental rule governing Starfleet's interactions with alien civilizations. It prohibits interference with the normal development of pre-warp civilizations.

general_order_1.text: Starfleet personnel are prohibited from interfering with the normal and natural development of alien worlds and cultures.
general_order_1.rationale: Interference with developing civilizations can cause irreversible harm to their cultural and technological development, potentially destroying their chance to reach the stars on their own terms.
scope: Pre-warp civilizations must not be contacted
Advanced technology must not be given to less developed cultures
Political systems must not be influenced
Religious beliefs must not be challenged or confirmed

exceptions.description: Rare exceptions to the Prime Directive are permitted under specific circumstances.
conditions: When the civilization has already achieved warp capability
When the civilization explicitly requests assistance
When a greater threat endangers both the civilization and Starfleet
When the Prime Directive itself would cause greater harm
When the civilization has already been contacted by another faction
exceptions.approval_required: Fleet Admiral or Starfleet Command authorization required for any exception

violation_consequences.description: Violating the Prime Directive is a serious offense with severe consequences.
penalties: Loss of commission and security clearance
Permanent damage to the affected civilization

game_mechanic.description: The Prime Directive affects diplomacy and exploration in the 4X game.
effects: Contacting pre-warp civilizations generates negative reputation
Violating the Prime Directive alerts other factions to your actions
Upholding the Prime Directive improves diplomatic standing with peaceful factions
Pre-warp civilizations can be observed but not directly interacted with

federation_history.description: The United Federation of Planets is a democratic interstellar federation founded on principles of peace, exploration, and mutual prosperity.

founding.context: After the Earth-Romulan war and the development of warp drive, Earth sought allies to ensure peace and stability in the region.

key_eras.name: Pre-Federation Era
key_eras.description: Earth develops warp drive, contacts Vulcans, and experiences the Xindi threat and Romulan conflicts.
events: First contact with Vulcans (2063, Zefram Cochrane)

key_eras.name: Early Federation
key_eras.description: The Federation expands, establishes Starfleet, and faces threats from the Klingons and Romulans.

key_eras.name: Original Series Era
key_eras.description: The era of the USS Enterprise (NCC-1701) under Captain Kirk. The Federation expands its influence and faces numerous threats.

key_eras.name: Next Generation Era
key_eras.description: The era of the USS Enterprise-D and E. The Federation faces the Borg, Dominion, and internal challenges.

key_eras.name: Modern Era
key_eras.description: The Federation continues to explore and defend against new threats, including the Emerald Chain and Burn-related anomalies.
events: The Burn - sudden disappearance of dilithium

branches.executive: President of the Federation, elected by the Federation Council

member_worlds: Many others across the Alpha and Beta Quadrants

major_conflicts.name: Klingon-Federation Border Wars
major_conflicts.description: A series of conflicts along the Federation-Klingon border, driven by territorial disputes and ideological differences.
major_conflicts.outcome: Khitomer Accords established peace, though tensions remain
major_conflicts.significance: Defined the relationship between the two major powers

major_conflicts.name: Dominion War
major_conflicts.description: A galactic-scale conflict between the Dominion (led by the Founders) and the Federation-Klingon-Romulan alliance.
major_conflicts.outcome: Alliance victory, Dominion retreats to the Gamma Quadrant
major_conflicts.significance: Major shift in galactic politics, strengthened Federation-Klingon alliance

major_conflicts.name: Borg Incursions
major_conflicts.description: Repeated attacks by the Borg Collective, a cybernetic species that assimilates other races.
key_battles: Battle of Sector 001 (Federation victory with help)
major_conflicts.significance: The Borg represent an existential threat to all sentient life

major_conflicts.name: Cardassian-Federation Border Conflict
major_conflicts.description: Tensions and conflicts along the Federation-Cardassian border, including the occupation of Bajor.
major_conflicts.outcome: Cardassian withdrawal from Bajor, establishment of Cardassian Federation
major_conflicts.significance: Led to the creation of Deep Space Nine as a diplomatic outpost

major_conflicts.name: Romulan-Federation Tensions
major_conflicts.description: Cold war-style tensions between the Federation and Romulan Star Empire, with proxy conflicts and espionage.
major_conflicts.significance: Defined the boundary between Federation and Romulan space

federation.name: United Federation of Planets
federation.description: A democratic interstellar federation dedicated to peace, exploration, and scientific discovery.
weaknesses: Reluctance to engage in preemptive warfare

klingon_empire.name: Klingon Empire
klingon_empire.description: A warrior culture that values honor, strength, and martial prowess.

romulan_star_empire.name: Romulan Star Empire
romulan_star_empire.description: A secretive empire that values deception, espionage, and strategic planning.

dominion.name: The Dominion
dominion.description: A ruthless empire controlled by the Founders (Changelings), using the Vorta as administrators and the Jem'Hadar as soldiers.
weaknesses: Changelings are vulnerable to specific weapons

borg.name: Borg Collective
borg.description: A cybernetic hive mind that assimilates other species, adding their technology and biology to the Collective.

cardassian_union.name: Cardassian Union
cardassian_union.description: A militaristic empire that values order, discipline, and expansion through occupation.

ferengi_alliance.name: Ferengi Alliance
ferengi_alliance.description: A profit-driven society that values commerce above all else.

bajor.name: Bajor
bajor.description: A small but strategically important world that recently gained independence from Cardassian occupation.

warp_drive.description: Faster-than-light propulsion system that enables interstellar travel.

levels.warp_6: 216 times light speed (cruising speed for Constitution-class)
levels.transwarp: Beyond warp 9, used by Borg and some experimental drives

cloaking_device.description: Technology that renders ships invisible to sensors and visual observation.
limitations: Cannot fire weapons while cloaked (without decloaking)

transporter.description: Technology that dematerializes matter and transmits it to another location for rematerialization.
limitations: Range limited by power and atmospheric conditions
Cannot transport living beings through planetary shields
Heisenberg compensator required for accurate rematerialization

replicator.description: Technology that converts energy into matter, allowing the creation of food, objects, and materials.
limitations: Cannot replicate certain complex materials (e.g., dilithium)

shields.description: Energy barriers that protect ships from weapons fire.

types.deflector_shields: Primary protection, can be directed to specific arcs
types.inertial_dampeners: Reduce effects of acceleration and deceleration
types.adaptive_shields: Borg technology that adapts to weapon frequencies

weapons.phasers: Energy weapons that can be set to stun or kill
weapons.photon_torpedoes: Antimatter warheads that explode on impact
weapons.quantum_torpedoes: More powerful variant of photon torpedoes
weapons.polaron: Less common energy weapon, effective against certain shields

key_locations.name: Earth
key_locations.description: Capital of the Federation, home to Starfleet Headquarters.
key_locations.significance: Political and military center of the Federation

key_locations.name: Deep Space Nine
key_locations.description: Space station near a stable wormhole to the Gamma Quadrant.
key_locations.significance: Strategic trade hub and diplomatic outpost

key_locations.name: Vulcan
key_locations.description: Homeworld of the Vulcans, founding member of the Federation.
key_locations.significance: Center of Vulcan logic and science

key_locations.name: Qo'noS
key_locations.significance: Political and military center of the Klingon Empire

key_locations.name: Romulus
key_locations.description: Capital of the Romulan Star Empire.
key_locations.significance: Political and military center of the Romulan Star Empire

key_locations.name: Bajor
key_locations.description: Small world near the wormhole, recently freed from Cardassian occupation.

key_locations.name: Cardassia Prime
key_locations.significance: Political and military center of the Cardassian Union

key_locations.name: Wormhole
key_locations.description: Stable wormhole connecting the Alpha and Gamma Quadrants.
key_locations.significance: Gateway to the Gamma Quadrant and the Dominion

key_locations.name: Borg Cube
key_locations.description: Massive cubic starship of the Borg Collective.
